_meta.purpose: Cross-reference index into docs/adr/ADR-007-tjr-strategy-definition.md, NOT a duplicate of it. ADR-007 remains the sole authoritative text for every question below -- externalRef cites the exact section/item so the original wording can never silently drift from what is recorded here. Verified directly against the current file content on 2026-07-25 (re-read in full immediately before creating this index, not assumed from memory).
_meta.verificationMethod: Direct grep for the section headers ('## C. Unknown or ambiguous rules', '## Direct questions requiring your approval before any implementation') followed by a full read of both numbered lists in the current file.
_meta.note: The 14 'direct questions' section is a condensed, cross-cutting restatement of the same underlying unknowns as the 35 Section C items -- it is NOT 14 additional, distinct unresolved facts. This index therefore creates exactly 35 UnresolvedQuestion records (one per Section C item, since that is the granular ledger this schema is built to track) plus a separate ownerApprovalQuestionGroups array below that maps each of the 14 direct questions to the Section C item(s) it consolidates, so both views of the ADR's own structure are preserved without double-counting or re-typing either list.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Exact pair list and any per-pair exceptions.
Exact session window(s) and whether they differ from JVM's.
Whether a news blackout is required, and if so, its data source.
The three (or more) timeframe roles and their actual values.
The exact bias-derivation rule and what makes a "neutral" (no-trade) state.
What counts as a valid liquidity level (equal-high/low tolerance in pips or %; whether session/day/week highs-lows all count or only some).
Internal vs. external liquidity distinction, if any, and whether it changes entry weighting.
The exact, objective sweep definition (wick-through vs. close-through; how many bars the close-back-inside must happen within).
The exact swing-point algorithm (lookback bars; strict vs. equal-high tolerance).
The exact structure-shift/break-of-structure definition (close-based vs. wick-based; minimum displacement size, in pips or ATR multiples).
The exact entry trigger (FVG minimum size and how staleness is defined; order-block selection rule if multiple exist; candle-confirmation requirement, if separate from the FVG/OB itself).
Limit vs. market entry, and -- if limit -- how long an unfilled limit order remains valid.
Maximum bars/time allowed between the sweep (or structure shift) and a valid entry.
Whether a "missed" entry (price ran past the zone without filling) may ever be chased, and if so, how.
Stop-loss placement rule and buffer (fixed pips? ATR-based? beyond the sweep wick?).
Minimum and maximum acceptable stop distance, if any.
Spread treatment in stop/target math (JVM fills at real bid/ask; does TJR need the same, and does spread affect stop placement itself?).
Target rule: fixed R-multiple, next opposing liquidity level, or something else.
Partial-exit rules, if any (size split, trigger price, whether MOGO's paper-account model even needs to support partials -- it doesn't today for JVM/ALEX).
Break-even rule (trigger condition, exact new stop price).
Trailing-stop rule, if any.
Maximum holding time and/or forced end-of-session closure rule.
Risk-per-trade percentage.
One-position-per-pair vs. a different concurrency rule.
Total concurrent-position cap across all pairs.
Daily loss limit / circuit breaker, if any (JVM and ALEX both currently have none enforced -- see docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md).
Maximum trades per session/day.
Correlated-pair exposure restrictions, if any.
Whether TJR is strictly pass/fail or scored; if scored, every component and its weight, and the minimum qualifying threshold -- none of this exists yet even as a shape.
Cooldown duration and same-liquidity-event re-trigger handling.
Re-entry rule after a stop-out or a missed target on the same setup.
Replay-specific tie-break for a candle that touches both stop and target (JVM's Replay engine has its own resolved convention -- does TJR reuse it or need its own?).
Spread/slippage assumption for Replay fills.
Warm-up history requirement (minimum candles before a decision is trusted) per timeframe.
Whether "incomplete" (still-forming) candles are ever evaluated, or only closed ones.

ownerApprovalQuestionGroups.summary: Which pairs should TJR scan -- JVM's 12, all 34, or a different list?
What are TJR's actual session windows, and does it need a news blackout?
What are the three (or more) timeframes, and what role does each play?
How is directional bias derived, and what makes it "neutral"?
What is the objective, numeric definition of a liquidity sweep (tolerance, close-back requirement, bar limit)?
What is the objective swing-point/structure-shift algorithm (lookback, wick vs. close, minimum displacement)?

What is the exact entry trigger (FVG/order block formation and invalidation rules; candle confirmation requirement; limit vs. market; max bars before the entry expires; whether a missed entry can be chased)?
What is the stop-loss placement rule and buffer, and are there min/max distance limits?
What is the target rule (fixed R, structural, partials, break-even, trailing, max hold time, forced session-close)?
What are the risk controls (risk %, concurrency limits, daily loss limit, max trades/day, correlated-pair restrictions)?
Is TJR pass/fail or scored -- and if scored, what are the components, weights, and threshold?
What are the cooldown and re-entry rules after a loss, a missed target, or a duplicate liquidity event?
What are the Replay-specific tie-break, spread/slippage, and warm-up history assumptions?
Should any of the above reuse an existing JVM/ALEX mechanism verbatim (e.g., session gate, ledger-commit pattern), or does TJR need its own for every item?
ownerApprovalQuestionGroups.notes: Cross-cutting -- does not map to a single Section C item; applies to all of them.
